summary: Audit log export to SIEM missing Dedicated rollout promote/abort event types (staged rollouts beta)
description:
Issue summary
- The audit log export pipeline (used for compliance export/SIEM forwarding) is not emitting the new Dedicated staged rollout action event types (promote/abort/hold/force-promote) introduced for the “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” project.

Context
- Dedicated staged rollouts beta is being enabled behind feature flags for a small set of accounts/pools (see INT-1933).
- The control plane emits audit events for actions (create/update/promote/abort, plus admin overrides). Console and internal tooling show these events in-line, but our export feed does not include them.
- This was raised during the enterprise security review expectations: customers (esp. regulated) require end-to-end auditability (Console + export/SIEM) for change-management controls.

Current behavior
- Events visible in Console audit trail / internal admin views.
- SIEM/exported audit stream is missing:
  - dedicated_pool_rollout.stage_promote
  - dedicated_pool_rollout.abort
  - dedicated_pool_rollout.hold / resume
  - dedicated_pool_rollout.force_promote (admin override)
- Export pipeline appears to be using an allowlist of event_type values; new types are being dropped.

Expected behavior
- All rollout action audit events are exported to the audit sink(s) with the same payload fields as other audit events (actor, actor_type, account_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, stage_from, stage_to, reason, request_id, idempotency_key, override flags).
- For compliance: exported events must be queryable by account_id + time window; retention unaffected.

Impact / risk
- Compliance gap for beta/GA: change-management evidence incomplete for Dedicated staged rollouts.
- Internal security review risk: any customer using SIEM export will not see rollout promotions/aborts, creating an audit trail discrepancy between Console and their compliance systems.
- Operational risk: oncall/post-incident analysis loses exported breadcrumbs (who promoted what stage when) if SIEM export is the source of truth.

Detection
- Kevin noticed missing event types while validating export coverage against the audit events spec page.
- Spot check: export topic contains create/update events for rollout plan objects, but not stage actions.

Steps to reproduce
1) Enable staged rollouts feature flag for a test Dedicated account/pool.
2) Create rollout plan and promote from stage 0 -> stage 1.
3) Confirm audit event appears in Console/audit API.
4) Check SIEM export stream for same request_id and event_type; event is absent.

Investigation notes (initial)
- Hypothesis: exporter has a static allowlist and needs to be updated with new event_type values.
- Secondary: payload mapping might be rejecting events due to new fields (stage_from/stage_to) not recognized by schema validator.
- Need to confirm whether events are dropped at source (producer), in the export consumer, or downstream in the delivery path.

Requested outcome
- Patch exporter allowlist + schema mapping; add coverage test(s) so new event types are not silently dropped.
- Backfill is not required for beta, but we should confirm whether we need retroactive export for any early beta actions (if any occurred in regulated contexts).

Acceptance criteria
- Promote/abort/hold/force-promote events appear in export within normal delivery latency.
- Exported payload includes stage transition data and actor attribution.
- Monitoring/alert added (or updated) for dropped/unknown audit event types (rate > 0 triggers ticket).

Owner(s)
- Primary: Kevin Osei (audit export/SIEM requirements)
- Supporting: Logan Wright (telemetry/audit pipeline), Kaitlyn Nguyen (RBAC/audit review)

resolution: Fixed audit exporter allowlist + schema mapping to include Dedicated staged rollout action event types (promote/abort/hold/force-promote). Verified in staging and prod that events appear in export stream with expected payload fields. Added alert/ticketing on unknown/dropped audit event types to prevent silent regressions. No backfill performed (beta-only exposure; no regulated customer actions identified during the gap window).
